question: Events $E_1,E_2,E_3$ form a partition of a sample space such that $P(E_1)=\frac14$, $P(E_2)=\frac12$ and $P(E_3)=\frac14$. For an event $A$, $P(A|E_1)=\frac15$, $P(A|E_2)=\frac25$ and $P(A)=\frac25$. Find $P(A|E_3)$.
explanation:
Step 1: Identification of the unknown probability
Let $P(A|E_3)=x$. The events $E_1,E_2,E_3$ form a partition, so the theorem of total probability can be applied.
Step 2: Total probability relation
$$P(A)=P(E_1)P(A|E_1)+P(E_2)P(A|E_2)+P(E_3)P(A|E_3)$$
Step 3: Substitution of the given values
$$\frac25=\frac14\times\frac15+\frac12\times\frac25+\frac14x$$
Step 4: Simplification
$$\frac25=\frac1{20}+\frac15+\frac{x}{4}=\frac14+\frac{x}{4}$$
Therefore, $$\frac{x}{4}=\frac25-\frac14=\frac{3}{20}$$ and hence $$x=\frac35.$$
Step 5: Conclusion
Thus, $$\boxed{P(A|E_3)=\frac35}.$$
